title: Cosmic Dawn
subtitle: From the CMB to the first light
description: Interactive exhibit on recombination, the cosmic microwave background, the dark ages, first stars and galaxies, reionization, JWST's early-galaxy frontier, and the cautious 21-cm radio search—linking conceptually to Cosmic Web without duplicating it.
source_note: Timeline epochs use approximate ages/redshifts with stated ranges. First-star properties and reionization details remain active research. 21-cm cosmology claims stay conservative. Stellarium shows present-day optical sky only—not the early Universe.
illustrative_disclaimer: ILLUSTRATIVE TIMELINE & REIONIZATION SKETCHES — educational transitions, not precision cosmology simulations unless separately labeled.

classification_legend.reconstruction: Processed maps/images reconstructed from observations (e.g. CMB all-sky maps)

science.hot_plasma: In the early Universe, matter was a hot ionized plasma tightly coupled to radiation. Photons scattered frequently off free electrons.
science.recombination: As the Universe cooled (roughly a few hundred thousand years after the Big Bang; redshift z~1100), electrons combined with nuclei into neutral atoms—recombination—and photon scattering plummeted.
science.cmb: Those freed photons form the cosmic microwave background: an all-sky microwave glow mapped by COBE, WMAP, and Planck. Maps are processed observations, not optical photographs.
science.dark_ages: After the CMB, before stars lit up, the Universe entered the dark ages: mostly neutral hydrogen, no starlight yet, while gravity continued amplifying density fluctuations.
science.first_stars: First stars (often called Population III) are expected from primordial H/He gas. Exact masses, multiplicity, and lifetimes remain uncertain research topics—not settled textbook numbers.
science.first_galaxies: Gas collected in growing dark-matter halos, formed stars, and assembled early galaxies through accretion and mergers—foreshadowing Cosmic Web structure.
science.reionization: Ionizing radiation from early luminous sources carved ionized bubbles that grew and overlapped until most intergalactic hydrogen became ionized. Timing and dominant sources remain active research (roughly first billion years; high redshift).
science.redshift: Cosmological redshift tracks expansion of space: light from earlier epochs arrives stretched. Higher redshift generally means looking farther back—not merely ordinary Doppler motion through static space.
science.twenty_one_cm: Neutral hydrogen's 21-cm line can in principle probe dark ages and reionization after cosmological redshift. Foregrounds make detection extremely hard; do not overstate current claims.
science.jwst: JWST observes highly redshifted galaxies. Photometric candidates need careful confirmation; 'earliest ever' headlines evolve as spectroscopy and models improve.

Distance–redshift relations depend on cosmological parameters; treat numbers as approximate.

twenty_one_cm.label: 21-cm COSMOLOGY — FRONTIER
twenty_one_cm.disclaimer: Concept and experimental challenge. Do not claim a definitive cosmological 21-cm detection map here. Foregrounds dominate.
points: Neutral hydrogen has a 21-cm hyperfine line.
Cosmological expansion shifts the line to lower observed frequencies.
In principle this probes dark ages and reionization.
Bright foregrounds make the measurement extraordinarily difficult.
Projects such as HERA, LOFAR, and SKA-pathfinders pursue this frontier.

narration.lookback: Looking deep into the sky is looking back in time. Cosmic Dawn is the era when the Universe made its first starlight after the afterglow of the Big Bang.
narration.recombination: As space cooled, electrons joined nuclei. Photons stopped scattering endlessly—and the Universe became transparent to light.
narration.cmb: That freed light is the cosmic microwave background: the oldest map we can draw of the whole sky.
narration.dark_ages: Then came the dark ages—not empty, but without stars. Gravity kept sculpting invisible hills of dark matter and gas.
narration.first_stars: Somewhere in those hills, the first stars ignited. Their exact sizes remain an open research question.
narration.first_galaxies: Galaxies grew from collapsing gas in dark-matter halos—the early chapters of the Cosmic Web story.
narration.reionization: Starlight and early galaxies carved ionized bubbles that grew until the fog of neutral hydrogen cleared.
narration.jwst: JWST peers toward that dawn with infrared eyes. Candidates need careful redshift checks as the frontier moves.
narration.twenty_one_cm: Radio astronomers listen for neutral hydrogen's 21-centimeter whisper—an extremely difficult, still-developing probe.
narration.closing: From microwave afterglow to first firelight, Cosmic Dawn bridges the hot beginning to the galaxies we map today.
